svg.title: The window remembers
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch of a twelve-cell array where the naive approach of recomputing every window of four is struck through in red and labelled n windows times k work; the same array with left and right pointer arrows under a highlighted window and a running sum of 14; the window advanced one cell with a green plus-arr-of-R arrow entering and a red minus-arr-of-L arrow leaving to give 15 in two operations; both pointers shown traversing the array exactly once for linear total work; and a prefix-sum row beneath the array with the formula P of j plus one minus P of i, annotated with measured timings of 503.8 milliseconds naive against 2.16 milliseconds with prefix sums.
svg.text: sum every window of 4 - the naive way
n windows x k work = O(nk)
you keep re-adding the same numbers
R moves one cell. Two operations, not four.
and each pointer only ever moves right
each pointer moves n times TOTAL => O(n), not O(n²)
measured: 503.8 ms naive range sums -> 2.16 ms with prefix sums = 233x
P[j+1] - P[i] = sum(i..j), in one subtraction
8.1 ms to build the prefix array. Then every query is free.
the window never recomputes what it
already knew. That sentence is the
